key_insight: Self-supervised pretraining can give neutrino-detector models a strong general-purpose starting point, making them better at classifying events, reconstructing signals, and adapting to different detector technologies. In short, the model learns useful physics features from unlabeled data before being fine-tuned for specific tasks.
problem_solved: Neutrino detectors produce highly complex, heterogeneous event data that is expensive to label and differs across detector technologies. This paper addresses the challenge of building models that are data-efficient, robust, and transferable across these diverse detector environments.
method: Pretrain deep learning models using self-supervised objectives on large amounts of unlabeled detector data.
Fine-tune the pretrained representations for downstream tasks such as event classification and reconstruction.
Evaluate transferability across heterogeneous neutrino detector technologies to test foundation-style behavior.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how self-supervised learning can reduce dependence on labeled data in scientific domains with expensive annotations. It also highlights a path toward reusable foundation-style models that generalize across related but different sensors or instruments.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing self-supervised pretraining -> fine-tuning -> downstream tasks
Side-by-side comparison of performance with and without pretraining
Illustration of different neutrino detector technologies connected by a shared embedding space
Icon-based summary of benefits: better classification, reconstruction, data efficiency, transfer
paper_title: Towards foundation-style models for energy-frontier heterogeneous neutrino detectors via self-supervised pretraining
paper_authors: Saúl Alonso-Monsalve, Fabio Cufino, Umut Kose, Anna Mascellani, André Rubbia
